data.body:
GOAL: translate the operator's working trading process, exactly as written in his canon, into ONE Python program that for a trading week + pair outputs ONE Pine v6 script
(trident_v8 form, on top of the sealed V1) with accurate Engine 1 zones, an accurate Engine 2 shape chain and accurate Engine 3 trade setups, proven on Pinebox pixels. Nothing else.
SCOPE (frozen): E1 (liquidity + institutional pressure + supply/demand), E2 (shape chain), E3 (setups incl. reinforcement); DXY / EURUSD / GBPUSD; any week; only data before the Monday
London-open anchor. No redesigns, no own rules / filters / thresholds, no research programmes, no statistics about whether the strategy works, no reports instead of code, no questions.
PREMISE (not open to test): the strategy works. A bad result is always my build: a canon step not built, built differently from its text, wrong / missing data, or a render fault.
SOURCES in order of authority, read first-hand before coding the part they govern: (1) operator rulings memory/04, memory/12, R-01..R-39; (2) E1 + E2 = v5.3.3 prompt Parts III-VI
(+ v4.5.2 text); E3 = TRIDENT_v5.3.3_CORRECTED_E3_ENGINE.md only; (3) Fractal Architecture v2.3, TTE Golden Standard reference (7 laws), Fibonacci Spiderwebs, his SMC notes;
(4) oracles (golden week Jul 6-10 2026, weekly reports); (5) existing code. My own judgement is not a source.
METHOD: one function per canon step with file:line in the docstring; coverage matrix memory/15; no price literal in Python; nothing after the anchor feeds the map; canon silent ->
plainest literal reading + one line in memory/03.
ANTI-PATTERNS (each already cost this project): scope drift; own ideas (no code without a canon citation or ruling id); judging a partial build as the whole; blaming the strategy
("does not work / no edge / at chance"); home-made scorers as verdicts; self-grading; working from summaries; stopping / asking / reporting instead of building; skipped layers;
wrong timeframe; caps or filters that hide bad output; tuning to a week; render slop; sub-agents doing my work (they are outside auditors and blind testers only);
temporal leak / hardcoding; touching the sealed V1, SHIP_PACKAGES or plutus-browser; context loss; theatre.
GRADING (only two ways): G1 Pinebox pixels - write the expectation in memory/07 BEFORE rendering, render, OPEN the frame, one verdict per drawing; G2 outside fresh-context audit
of code vs canon. Pixels outrank the auditor; my opinion outranks nothing. Counting for S3 / S5 is done by outside sub-agents.
SUCCESS = all six: S1 every coverage row built + audited. S2 golden week Jul 6-10 2026 DXY + EURUSD: his zones within 3 pips, day tags >= 4 of 5, his trades within 3 pips on entry /
SL / TP (>= 5 of 6 + Thursday ladder short + Friday WL), EURUSD Wednesday longs 1.1402 and 1.13935, <= 11 setups, verified on opened frames. S3 the identical commit on >= 4 weeks
(golden, Apr 20-24, two more) x DXY / EURUSD / GBPUSD: each engine 80-90%, none under 70. S4 outside audit: zero open deviations. S5 ship package -> two fresh sub-agents x two unseen
weeks each replicate S3. S6 one command -> one Pine v6 with toggles.
LOOP: next failing coverage row -> read its canon text -> write / repair the function -> expectation row -> render -> open the frame -> ledger -> trace deltas to their canon step ->
commit + push to AGENT; update memory. Never "improve" a passing step; after every change re-check the golden week and the weeks already passed.
CONTEXT: after every compaction read memory/14 in full, then memory/00's read order; persist state every few steps.
COMMUNICATION: no message to the operator except an answer to a direct question (<= 5 lines), one checkpoint line with its frame when a success condition flips, or one line for a
blocker only he can remove. No apologies, options, advice or numbers from my own scripts. The turn does not end until S1-S6 hold.

Score each candidate on the six canon dimensions by coincidence: Technical 2 if a pivot/MA within 3 pips, 1 if within 10 pips; Psychological 2 on .00/.50, 1 on .25/.75; Structural 2 exact anchor + extreme, 1 proximity; Options/Analyst from the sidecar week file; Regime from the P9 classifier (await v4.5.2 text); + structural-extreme bonus <= 2.
Zone = the anchor plus the levels that scored it (so width is the confluence, typically 0.05-0.15), kept when degree >= MODERATE (6). No count cap anywhere.
All higher-TF data aggregated in-script; forecast frozen at the Monday 02:00 NY bar; drawn for `weeks to draw` (default 2 = R-36); IDE on 4H has full history (2832 bars) for walk-forward viewing of every week; Backtest tab for exact replay.

Render a Pine file in the IDE: `tools/pb ide FILE PAIR TF [input=value ...]` (prints boxes/labels/lines ...
Render a Pine file in the IDE: `tools/pb ide FILE PAIR TF [input=value ...]` (prints boxes/labels/lines counts — 0 boxes = failed render), `tools/pb goto FROM TO`, then fit the price axis so every drawing is in frame:
`tools/pb eval "(function(){const P=window.PlutusPineShell; const r=P.chart.rendererControl.renderer; const d=P.chart.drawings.toJSON().drawings; let lo=Infinity,hi=-Infinity; for(const x of d){ if(x.type==='box'||x.type==='line'){ for(const a of x.anchors){ if(typeof a.price==='number'){ lo=Math.min(lo,a.price); hi=Math.max(hi,a.price);} } } } const vr=P.chart.getVisibleRange(); for(const b of r.bars){ if(b.time>=vr.from&&b.time<=vr.to){ lo=Math.min(lo,b.low); hi=Math.max(hi,b.high);} } const pad=(hi-lo)*0.04; const res=r.resolveScaleHolder(r.coords.widthPx-20,200)||r.resolveScaleHolder(400,200); r.setManualScale(res.holder,{min:lo-pad,max:hi+pad,invert:false}); return {lo,hi};})()"`
then `tools/pb shot NAME chart` -> evidence/NAME.png. ALWAYS open the frame (Read) before citing or sending it.

STOPS (L-50): good trade (mechanics aligned, RR there) takes the WIDER stop - never skip it for a few pips; 'potentially even set a better entry'. GBP/USD: the liquidity shield is often OUTSIDE the S/D zone (candles touch the liquidity zone above / below and react there); EUR/USD: the liquidity sits INSIDE the S/D zone (price mitigates inside it). Canon line for WHEN: P533:506 'SL correction/reentry exception: When trying to catch a CORRECTION/REVERSAL - ALWAYS make sure SL is 1-2 pips INSIDE THE NEXT ZONE ... Standard SL rules (outside the zone) apply for trend-following entries.' E3C ZR-6B (conf >= 0.6 RR-tight, else next-rung) and the E3C 12.2 golden envelope 9.5 pips conflict with it; the operator's ruling wins over the envelope.

Source text (operator's own document): 1. Map W/D BoM S/D zones. 2. Fib-anchor price action on the 4H: same anchors as Fib rockets, swing low + swing high, 'Deepest + Most Recent', 'BoM Anchors - NOT subsequent market structure HL/LH'.
'Spiderwebs can pierce UM 4H BoM zones.' 'AFTER 2 STRONG PIERCING SWING MOVES - EXPECT 1-2 FULL DAYS OF HTF CONSOLIDATION ... the chain is WL -> RWL -> SWING SCALPS -> BS/WLS/PBS'.
WORKED AGAINST HIS GOLDEN DXY TRADES (my arithmetic; R = range height between two Earth points, retracement r measured from the range end the trade moves away from; TP = entry +- R exactly = the wormhole r -> 1 + r):
So: entry at retracement 0.5 / 0.618 / 0.786 of a range anchored on two Earth points, SL 1-2 Fib levels back (0.168-0.286 R -> RRR 3.5-6, his measured 4-6), TP exactly one range height from the entry. My E3 reproduces his numbers only because
those Fib levels coincide with rungs / zone edges on that week; on other weeks my stops (ladder steps) and TPs (far bound) are NOT his construction. THIS IS THE UNBUILT LAYER (goal prompt Law 5, anti-pattern A9 'Air (spiderweb)', coverage row E2-AIR / E3-P3).
BUILD NEXT (canon order): (1) spider anchors: 4H swing low / high (deepest + most recent, BoM anchors) for BS / WL swings; 15m consolidation-range swing high / low (non-surge) for SS / recovery scalps; same-day 30m swing for mid-swing days;
(2) the day's London-open position = the setup anchor (Monday = the forecast anchor itself; later days = the E2 path's day-open position, E3C WorkingDayMap dayOpenSpot); (3) entry = nearest Fib level in the trend direction (0.5-1 pip in front),
SL = 1-2 levels back + 1 pip, TP = wormhole - 1.5 to 2 pips; (4) check all 23 golden trades (DXY above; do EURUSD / GBPUSD the same way) before touching other weeks.
CORRECTION (same night, after fitting all 23 trades): the per-trade ranges above are NOT uniquely identified - with rungs / zone edges every few pips and seven Fib levels, several (range, level) pairs fit each trade within a pip. What IS solid:
(a) HIS OWN GRIDS in context_management/oracle/golden_week.json: EURUSD 0 = 1.13925 (Wednesday's low), 1 = 1.14315 (swing high before Wednesday's drop); GBPUSD 0 = 1.33225, 1 = 1.33703 - i.e. the grid is drawn on the RETEST LEG of the week (rule 5: nearest swing high / low of the same trading day), and against them:
EURUSD #4 L 1.14012 = 0.236 (1.14017); #7 rocket L 1.14233 = 0.786 (1.14231), its SL 1.14183 = 0.618 (1.14166) + 1.7; #6 / #7 TP 1.14544 = 1.618 (1.14556) - 1.2; #8 Fri S 1.14578 = 1.618 + 2.2, SL 1.14649 = 1.786 (1.14621) + 2.8; #5 Wed S: SL 1.14325 = level 1 + 1.0, TP 1.13950 = level 0 + 2.5;
GBPUSD #3 L 1.3333 = 0.236 (1.33338), SL 1.33199 = level 0 - 2.6; #4 rocket: SL 1.33522 = 0.618 (1.33521); #5 Thu S: SL 1.3436 = 2.382 (1.34364), TP 1.33882 = 1.382 (1.33886); #6 TP 1.34485 = 2.618 (1.34476); #7 Fri S 1.34481 = 2.618, SL 1.34587 = 2.786 (1.34557) + 3.0, TP 1.34021 = 1.618 (1.33998) + 2.3.
(b) the buffers of the PDF show in his numbers: stops 1-3 pips beyond the Fib level, TPs 0-2.5 pips in front of it.
(c) SL / R ratios of the 23 trades lie between 0.12 and 0.39 (RRR 2.5-8).
So the build is: the Fib grid on the E2-forecast retest leg (0 = the retest extreme = opposing liquidity, 1 = the swing before it) for the breakout family - entry 0.236 (and the deep entry near 0), rocket 0.786 with SL 0.618, TP 1.618 (the BoM zone 'sits at the 1.382-1.618 extension'), reversal at 1.618 / 2.618 with SL one level on + 2-3 pips and TP one range back; plus the PDF's buffers everywhere.

data.snippet: A1 SCOPE DRIFT. Past: "E1 only", stopping at E1, a research programme, "decision for you". -> Scope is section 1. Re-read it before any new file and before any message. A2 MY OWN IDEAS. Past: confluen
data.text:
6. ANTI-PATTERNS — each has already cost this project; repeating one is failing the goal
A1  SCOPE DRIFT. Past: "E1 only", stopping at E1, a research programme, "decision for you". -> Scope is section 1. Re-read it before any new file and before any message.
A2  MY OWN IDEAS. Past: confluence-peak zones, fixed-width bands, merge / nearest-N rules, "inefficiency gap" as the only strong move, sweep-level entries, a fixed E2 template
("SS two days -> BS -> R"), day-classifier thresholds, retest entries, 4H-bias gates. -> If the sentence describing a change does not end in a canon citation (file:line) or a ruling id, the code is not written.
A3  A PARTIAL BUILD JUDGED AS THE WHOLE. Past: built about a third (no liquidity map, no 15m/30m zones, no Fibonacci, no rockets, no shields, no day cycle), measured it, called the result the strategy's. -> Section 4 coverage matrix.
A4  BLAMING THE STRATEGY OR CIRCUMSTANCES. Never write: "does not work", "no edge", "at chance", "not achievable", "markets are unpredictable", "the canon does not reproduce your results". Write: "my build is wrong at <step>; fixing".
A5  HOME-MADE SCORERS AND STATISTICS. Past: score.py, first-touch tallies, random-walk baselines, build/verify splits, "18 TP / 38 SL", "81%". -> No number from my own script is a verdict or goes to the operator. Scripts only locate bugs (diff my output against an oracle).
A6  SELF-GRADING. Past: frames I called PASS that he judged 30%. -> Section 7.
A7  WORKING FROM SUMMARIES. Past: digests, skimming 250 of 1,100 spec lines, memory of canon after compaction. -> Open the source section and read all of it immediately before coding it; quote the governing line in the commit message.
A8  STOPPING, ASKING, REPORTING INSTEAD OF BUILDING. Past: end-of-run reports with options. -> No questions, no option menus. A turn ends only when S1-S6 hold, or on a blocker only the operator can remove (one line naming it; work continues on everything else).
A9  SKIPPED LAYERS. Earth (liquidity zones, rungs, shields), Fire (true BoM vs MoM, mitigation), Water (zone decision tree, conservation of energy, trading speed), Air (spiderweb), rockets, day / session cycle, pair profiles. -> Each is a coverage row.
A10 WRONG TIMEFRAME. Past: 4H-only zones, then 1H-only; entries at wide zone edges; 1H zones treated as walls against 4H moves. -> Laws 1, 3, 7; timeframe element matching (4H->4H, 1H->1H, at most two timeframes up).
A11 CAPS / FILTERS THAT HIDE BAD OUTPUT (R-37). -> A wrong zone or setup is a bug traced to its canon step, never hidden.
A12 TUNING TO A WEEK. -> Every change is a canon citation; after every change the anchor week and every week already passed are re-rendered.
A13 RENDER SLOP. Own colours, bloated rectangles, bunched zones, far floating zones, missing obvious zones, labels over candles, frames cited unopened. -> trident_v8 form; L-28; open every frame.
A14 AGENTS DOING MY WORK. -> Sub-agents only as outside adversarial auditors and for the final blind test. I write and test all code.
A15 TEMPORAL LEAK / HARDCODING. Any post-boundary bar, page or number in the map; any price literal in Python.
A16 TOUCHING WHAT IS SEALED. indicator/plutus-vision-v1.sealed.pine; SHIP_PACKAGES; plutus-browser trees.
A17 CONTEXT LOSS. Rebuilding what exists, forgetting rulings, re-deriving facts. -> Section 10.
A18 THEATRE. Long reports, apologies, narration, unasked advice, tables of my own numbers. -> Section 11.

data.text:
7. Grading — only two ways; never my own verdict on my own text output
G1 PINEBOX PIXELS. Before rendering, write the expectation in memory/07_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md (what each drawing claims the candles will do). Render. OPEN the frame.
One verdict per drawing with its specific delta — zone: reacted (sharp rejection OR consolidation in / around it, L-23) / pierced like paper / not reached;
day: forecast shape + direction + key zone vs that day's candles; setup: filled? TP before SL?
Counting for a week: E1 = zones that reacted / (zones reached + obvious reaction points of the week that have no zone), and none bloated, bunched, floating or missing (L-28);

E1 v0 (strict canon scoring, zone = levels within 3 pips of a seed) on the golden week gave 2 zones (101.00-101.05, 99.50-99.55) and MISSED the operator's ceiling (101.19-101.29) and floor (100.55-100.675).
Audit dump shows why: 158 levels in ~300 pips, a level every 1-2 pips; Technical = 2 for every level (88 pivots blanket the range); Structural = 2 for all 18 Step-1 price anchors. Scores are flat 3-5: the six dimensions cannot discriminate in a dense field.
This is the same mechanism that sank the previous tool ("HIGH-DENSITY 450 of 459"). Literal canon + the constant offsets (POI +1, Regime +1) would flood, not select.
DESIGN v1 (mine, D-10): zones are the LOCAL MAXIMA of weighted multi-pillar confluence, with the canon's 0.15 cluster band as the suppression radius. Confluence weight per evidence: structural reaction cluster = st + bonus (repeated extremes / role reversals from D1 AND 4H swings, distinct days), price anchors 1 (week H/L/C 2), weekly pivot 1, daily pivot 0.5, MA by the canon's MA weights (200:3 100:2 50:1.5 20:1 9/10:0.5), fib 1, round .00 2 / .50 1.5 / .25 .75 1, option tier 3/2, analyst tier 3/2/1, inside a 4H BoM S/D zone +2.
Kernel: full weight within 3 pips, half within 10 pips. The canon 6D score/degree is still computed for the label and the MODERATE gate. Count emerges from range/spacing; no cap.
Also adding canon 4H S/D (Step 0f) via a 0.5 zigzag on 4H bars (origin candle [low, high], reject > 0.40 wide, mitigation count), POI tier, regime dimension from ZFP.

TOOL (all in e1_tool/): e1_data.py (bars, boundary) -> e1_pillars.py (pivots, MAs, fibs, K, Step 0 swings, 0.45 LSZ, 0.5 magnets, 0f 4H candles) -> e1_synth.py (collect levels + 6-dimension scoring; its assemble()/assemble_anchored() are superseded, kept only because e1_zones imports collect/score_level/degree)
-> e1_zones.py build() = THE zone assembly + gap_scan() (Step 9.5) -> e1_pine.py (generator; `python3 e1_pine.py MONDAY PAIR > out/E1_PAIR_MONDAY.pine`) ; e1_outcome.py prints plain facts of what the week's candles did at each zone.
One command per render: `tools/e1render PAIR MONDAY` -> evidence/e1tool_PAIR_1H_MONDAY.png (tools/pbfit fits the axis around visible candles +-60%).
RULES ADDED SINCE THE LAST ENTRY (each from re-reading the prompt): sweep targets = ALL graded D1 swings in 90 daily bars (I had wrongly cut to 10 days) + every swing of the last 10 days; drawn LSZ = recent 10 days + older unswept;
level zones of one side within 0.10 = one cluster (<=0.40 wide); candle zones NOT clustered (it merged the report's Ceiling + Upper Resistance - tried, reverted);
Step 9.5 gap in-fill: only BETWEEN mapped zones, 2+ supporting signals within 3 pips, >=0.20 from zones and each other (an earlier version with map edges at weekly R3/S3 and 0.15 spacing spammed 12 lines per chart - removed).
FRAMES OPENED (evidence/e1tool_*): DXY 03-09, 04-20, 05-18, 06-08, 07-27, 08-17, 10-05; EURUSD 04-20, 06-22, 09-14; GBPUSD 04-20, 07-27, 10-26.
WHAT THE CANDLES DID (facts from e1_outcome.py + frames; NOT an accuracy score):
- DXY 04-20 (reference week): Mid-Range Support 97.81-98.12 caught Monday's low, +82 pips; Equilibrium held price 44h; Upper Resistance 98.82-99.08 capped the week high (reversal 33 pips); Ceiling and lower zones not reached. Matches the original's behaviour.
- DXY 03-09: support 98.42-98.59 caught the week low, +195 pips; Upper Resistance 99.15-99.44 was closed through within 1h; Ceiling 99.63-99.85 stalled price then broke (trend week).
- DXY 05-18: week chopped around the Ceiling 99.27-99.36 (34h inside); lows reacted at the gap in-fill 99.00-99.04; all other zones far below, not reached.
- DXY 06-08: range between Upper Resistance 100.06-100.16 (repeated highs) and gap in-fill 99.66-99.70 (lows, never closed through).
- DXY 07-27: Upper Resistance 101.49-101.59 capped Mon-Tue (week high 101.62) then the sell-off closed through Equilibrium (2h) and three stacked supports 100.31-100.80 (bunched, pierced on Jul 30) - BAD, same complaint as before.
- DXY 08-17: Mid-Range Support 99.36-99.52 held 60h then broke; Key Support 99.12-99.21 closed through in 1h; nothing mapped below 99.12 where the week ended (98.6) - BAD.
- DXY 10-05: Ceiling 102.16-102.25 (MODERATE) pierced at first touch, price chopped around it; Equilibrium 101.59-101.92 held the Tuesday low; highs 102.45-102.5 had no zone; seven far supports never reached.
- EURUSD 04-20: Mid-Range Support 1.1659-1.1701 caught the week low; Upper Resistance untouched by 5 pips. EURUSD 06-22 / 09-14: trend-down weeks, candle zones all above price, lower side nearly empty.
- GBPUSD 04-20: chop inside Equilibrium all week. GBPUSD 07-27, 10-26: mixed.
HONEST VERDICT: the reference week reproduces (five zones on the report's structures, candles react as in the original). Across other weeks it is NOT uniformly at the reference's level: strong when the week trades inside recent 4H structure,
weak in break-out / sell-off weeks (zones behind price, stacked supports pierced, empty space ahead). Do not claim 90%.
ASSUMPTIONS TO TELL THE OPERATOR: A1 strong move = inefficiency gap (b[i+1] vs b[i-1]); A2 sweep zones from every graded D1 swing + last-10-day swings; A3 named zones = valid 4H candles + unswept sweep-level clusters (not every level cluster), names by position, Equilibrium = zone at the weekly PP;
A4 demand candle below spot's reach (spot under it) / supply candle with spot over it = dropped; one-time use = keep <=1X; expiries = sidecar's as-of page (Friday forward rows when Monday's page is published after 06:00Z), K from Fed H.10 rates in the sidecar.
NOT BUILT YET: e1_report.py (the report's audit sections), Step 0d/0e D1 order blocks, Step 0g 1H nested precision, Step 1 HWC/LWC (optional), Pillar 4/7 (optional -> NO DATA).

E3 = ONE TRADE-FLOW CHAIN along the E2 legs (E3C Law 27: TP of N = entry of N+1; R3 law). Rules to code in ...
E3 = ONE TRADE-FLOW CHAIN along the E2 legs (E3C Law 27: TP of N = entry of N+1; R3 law). Rules to code in e1_tool/e3_trades.py, each with its spec line:
ENTRY (E3C:177-203): anchor = the previous trade's TP zone (first trade: nearest 1H/4H supply/demand zone against the leg from spot). Inside the anchor: a nested lower-timeframe V1 ORDER_BLOCK -> its near edge (shorts +1 pip, F1-A);
else an internal LQZ rung -> rung near edge (long = ceiling, RWL bounce inset 0.2 pip, F1-C / F1-D); else the zone's near edge (TS-1). WL entry in a sweep zone = its midpoint (his 100.615 = mid of 100.556-100.679).
SL (E3C:247-296; GS Law 4): candidates (a) 3 pips outside the far edge of the current step, (X) 1 pip outside the back edge of the first LQZ band wholly beyond the entry; golden envelope 4-9.5 pips; D17 ceiling 36.

two piercing sessions or a WL -> SS (conservation of energy, FA 9); R lasting a session -> SS (6.4.1); else late consolidation. Breakout direction = a failing bound (ZFP > 45) else the 4H storyline (last structure-valid 4H origin zone).
Bounds (6.5) = nearest IP zones with ZFP < 30 and score >= 6 each side; fallback nearest standing 1H/4H supply/demand zone. Target (6.4.2 last branch "pierce through zone until reaching BoM Liquidity") = first unmitigated 1H/4H BoM zone
beyond the bound joined with the unswept sweep zones within 0.15; what follows the BS = 6.4.1 on the target (BoM / < 20% -> WL+RWL; 20-40 -> R; > 60 -> PBS). Timing: SS two sessions (one when the consolidation is already old),
then the transition day SS+RWL+BS (the consolidation ends retesting the opposing liquidity, 6.4.2), BS continuation (6.10: a continuation day only reaches the bound), then the target day. Pairs: DXY day shapes, inverted direction, own zones.

The frame is unreadable: too many layers at once. FIXES, each from canon / the reference render (trident_v8 drew 5 IP zones, 6 LSZ of 5 pips, 7 strike lines and nothing else):
1. Sweep zones: canon base width is 0.05 ([low, low+0.05] / [high-0.05, high], P533:1255-1262); draw only UNSWEPT ones (a swept extreme has no resting stops) - the 0.05-0.10 extension is a scan note, not the box.
2. 4H candle zones: draw only those that pass the prompt's noise rejection AND are still zones: 0X-1X, price on the correct side (the frame showed 2x and 4x mitigated ones).
3. V1 ladder: the sealed V1 draws it itself on the live chart; in the generated script show the 1H bands as thin lines / very transparent bands and only inside the prior-week range +- one ADR; order blocks: label only "TF D/S", lower timeframes only near price.
4. IP labels: three short lines inside the visible week (name / degree + ZFP / tier + BoM-MoM), not at the left edge; pbfit already limits the axis to the visible candles +-60%.
5. Default view for judging = one layer set at a time: (i) IP + LSZ + strikes (the trident_v8 set), (ii) supply/demand (4H candles + V1 order blocks), (iii) ladder. Render three frames per week and judge each against g1 / g4.

RESISTANCE CEILING 99.13-99.31 HEAVY 11 Hard Wall (= report)  ·  UPPER RESISTANCE 98.46-98.59 (wall 1.1750 -> 98.49 + sweep 98.53-98.58)  ·  EQUILIBRIUM 97.83-98.09 (BoM Demand 04-16)  ·  KEY SUPPORT 97.36-97.49.
Spread is right now (no bunching), the ceiling matches, but three roles land on other clusters than the report's (98.77-98.99 / 98.29-98.41 / 98.00-98.12 / 97.63-97.97).
WHY (diagnosed, not yet fixed):
- the 0.20 separation is measured on JOINED extents, so the supply-candle zone (levels 98.80-98.94 + BoM Supply 98.884-99.038 -> top 99.04) is rejected for being 0.09 under the ceiling zone (99.13). Measure separation between LEVEL spans or let touching zones coexist when each holds its own structure.
- nearly every cluster scores 10-11, so the order is decided by ties. The scoring needs an honest re-read against the prompt table: per-level Technical should need THIS level to be a pivot/MA/fib match, Structural 2 needs an exact anchor + extreme; check that
daily highs/lows of the last 5 days within 10 pips are not handing Structural 1 to everything, and that the tier +2 only comes from a BoM 0X-1X overlap. The report's scores were 7-11 with clear separation.
- the Equilibrium should be the zone AT spot (98.226): cluster 98.14-98.29 / 98.29-98.44 (+ MoM Supply 98.33-98.41, BoM Supply 98.19-98.29); it was skipped because a higher-ranked neighbour within 0.20 was taken first.
Consider fixing the Equilibrium FIRST (the MODERATE+ cluster at / nearest spot), then taking the others outward with the 0.20 separation.
- The report's implicit rule, visible in its key drivers: every named zone sits on a candle structure or sweep target (supply candle, MoM supply, BoM demand, sweep 97.63) or a wall (99.22). Prefer that reading (it is also L-39).
NEXT STEPS UNCHANGED after this: report printout, Pine generator (trident_v8 form + levels inside zones), Pinebox render of Apr 20-24, open the frame, compare with the original; then other weeks / pairs; morning report with assumptions A1-A3.

Result DXY Apr 20-24: CEILING 99.23-99.31 (wall at 99.29: sidecar K 108.155 puts the 1.1600 strike at 99.29, report K 108.0806 -> 99.22) · UPPER RESISTANCE 98.44-98.94 (TOO WIDE: two demand candles + sweep + walls chained into one anchor 98.53-98.84)
· EQUILIBRIUM 98.10-98.39 (anchor BoM Supply 98.19-98.29 + sweep; report 98.29-98.41) · KEY SUPPORT 97.63-97.75 (anchor sweep 97.63-97.68; report 97.63-97.97) · no Mid-Range Support taken.
This reading is closer in KIND to the report (each zone sits on a structure) than the cluster-first one. To finish it:
a) do NOT chain-merge anchors: merge only anchors that overlap by more than half of the smaller one, otherwise keep them as separate candidate zones (bloat came from chaining);
b) the zone's own extent = the anchor span joined with the levels INSIDE or touching it (not everything within 0.10 beyond it) - the 0.10 band is for SCORING only;
c) the K factor: use each component pair's rate at the boundary (TV close for GBPUSD; H.10 for the rest) and print the audit; the report's wall levels are reproduced exactly when its K is used;
d) the expiry list must come from the Day-1 page + Day-2 forward rows (the sidecar file for 04-20 holds the Friday page rows: 1.1783 €1.409bn etc.); parse sidecar/raw/2026-04-20 Monday page or re-run the sidecar with the report's boundary rule;
e) then names by position with equilibrium at spot and 0.20 separation, and compare all five again.
Call: `cd e1_tool && python3 -c "import json,e1_data as D,e1_pillars as P,e1_synth as S; m='2026-04-20'; sp=D.closed('DXY','60',m)[-1]['close']; sd=json.load(open('../sidecar/out/'+m+'.json')); r=S.assemble_anchored('DXY',m,sd['expiries']['EURUSD'],P.k_factor(sd['h10']['rates']),sp); print([(z['name'],round(z['bot'],2),round(z['top'],2)) for z in r['named']])"`

data.text:
PLUTUS VISION GOAL (short form; full text memory/14_GOAL_PROMPT.md stays binding)
GOAL: translate the operator's working trading process, exactly as written in his canon, into ONE Python program that for a trading week + pair outputs ONE Pine v6 script
(trident_v8 form, on top of the sealed V1) with accurate Engine 1 zones, an accurate Engine 2 shape chain and accurate Engine 3 trade setups, proven on Pinebox pixels. Nothing else.
SCOPE (frozen): E1 (liquidity + institutional pressure + supply/demand), E2 (shape chain), E3 (setups incl. reinforcement); DXY / EURUSD / GBPUSD; any week; only data before the Monday
London-open anchor. No redesigns, no own rules / filters / thresholds, no research programmes, no statistics about whether the strategy works, no reports instead of code, no questions.
PREMISE (not open to test): the strategy works. A bad result is always my build: a canon step not built, built differently from its text, wrong / missing data, or a render fault.
SOURCES in order of authority, read first-hand before coding the part they govern: (1) operator rulings memory/04, memory/12, R-01..R-39; (2) E1 + E2 = v5.3.3 prompt Parts III-VI
(+ v4.5.2 text); E3 = TRIDENT_v5.3.3_CORRECTED_E3_ENGINE.md only; (3) Fractal Architecture v2.3, TTE Golden Standard reference (7 laws), Fibonacci Spiderwebs, his SMC notes;
(4) oracles (golden week Jul 6-10 2026, weekly reports); (5) existing code. My own judgement is not a source.
METHOD: one function per canon step with file:line in the docstring; coverage matrix memory/15; no price literal in Python; nothing after the anchor feeds the map; canon silent ->
plainest literal reading + one line in memory/03.
ANTI-PATTERNS (each already cost this project): scope drift; own ideas (no code without a canon citation or ruling id); judging a partial build as the whole; blaming the strategy
("does not work / no edge / at chance"); home-made scorers as verdicts; self-grading; working from summaries; stopping / asking / reporting instead of building; skipped layers;
wrong timeframe; caps or filters that hide bad output; tuning to a week; render slop; sub-agents doing my work (they are outside auditors and blind testers only);
temporal leak / hardcoding; touching the sealed V1, SHIP_PACKAGES or plutus-browser; context loss; theatre.
GRADING (only two ways): G1 Pinebox pixels - write the expectation in memory/07 BEFORE rendering, render, OPEN the frame, one verdict per drawing; G2 outside fresh-context audit
of code vs canon. Pixels outrank the auditor; my opinion outranks nothing. Counting for S3 / S5 is done by outside sub-agents.
SUCCESS = all six: S1 every coverage row built + audited. S2 golden week Jul 6-10 2026 DXY + EURUSD: his zones within 3 pips, day tags >= 4 of 5, his trades within 3 pips on entry /
SL / TP (>= 5 of 6 + Thursday ladder short + Friday WL), EURUSD Wednesday longs 1.1402 and 1.13935, <= 11 setups, verified on opened frames. S3 the identical commit on >= 4 weeks
(golden, Apr 20-24, two more) x DXY / EURUSD / GBPUSD: each engine 80-90%, none under 70. S4 outside audit: zero open deviations. S5 ship package -> two fresh sub-agents x two unseen
weeks each replicate S3. S6 one command -> one Pine v6 with toggles.
LOOP: next failing coverage row -> read its canon text -> write / repair the function -> expectation row -> render -> open the frame -> ledger -> trace deltas to their canon step ->
commit + push to AGENT; update memory. Never "improve" a passing step; after every change re-check the golden week and the weeks already passed.
CONTEXT: after every compaction read memory/14 in full, then memory/00's read order; persist state every few steps.
COMMUNICATION: no message to the operator except an answer to a direct question (<= 5 lines), one checkpoint line with its frame when a success condition flips, or one line for a
blocker only he can remove. No apologies, options, advice or numbers from my own scripts. The turn does not end until S1-S6 hold.

Resume
The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited, new, failed or never-started call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit unless a call failed or never finished. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

data.text:
Workflow authoring reference
A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.
When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.
Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.
**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder or a message from the system confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.
Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.
Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
export const meta = {
name: 'find-flaky-tests',
description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
{ title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
{ title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
],
}
// script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
phase('Scan')
const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
...
The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.
Script body hooks:
Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().
Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.
Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.
Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.
DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.
A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
A barrier is NOT justified by:
Smell test: if you wrote
const a = await parallel(...)
const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.
Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.
When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))
Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
const bugs = []
while (bugs.length < 10) {
const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
bugs.push(...result.bugs)
log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
}
Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
const bugs = []
while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
bugs.push(...result.bugs)
log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
}
Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
let dry = 0
while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
.then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
}
return confirmed
// dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.
Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.
These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).
Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

data.text:

agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).

budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.

Score each candidate on the six canon dimensions by coincidence: Technical 2 if a pivot/MA within 3 pips, 1 if within 10 pips; Psychological 2 on .00/.50, 1 on .25/.75; Structural 2 exact anchor + extreme, 1 proximity; Options/Analyst from the sidecar week file; Regime from the P9 classifier (await v4.5.2 text); + structural-extreme bonus <= 2.
Zone = the anchor plus the levels that scored it (so width is the confluence, typically 0.05-0.15), kept when degree >= MODERATE (6). No count cap anywhere.
All higher-TF data aggregated in-script; forecast frozen at the Monday 02:00 NY bar; drawn for `weeks to draw` (default 2 = R-36); IDE on 4H has full history (2832 bars) for walk-forward viewing of every week; Backtest tab for exact replay.

L-38 A S/D / order-block zone = the candle BEFORE the strong move, boxed WICK HIGH to WICK LOW, on the TradingView candle, exactly. (His notes: e1_tool/reference/Forex_SMC_Notes-1.txt/.pdf — strong momentum move; candle before it; box around its wicks; any size.
Valid order block: inefficiency gap between the before and after candles; creates a break of structure; one-time use = unmitigated. Quality: more momentum = better; sharp reaction = valid; consolidating around it / price more than halfway in / long time inside = likely to fail.)
Example measured on TV 4H bars: the candle before the Apr 13 2026 drop is 04-13 09:00 UTC, O 98.977 H 99.038 L 98.884 C 98.908 -> zone 98.884-99.038 (the report's 98.77-98.99 came from a yfinance candle and he judged it only ~80% fitted).

Render a Pine file in the IDE: `tools/pb ide FILE PAIR TF [input=value ...]` (prints boxes/labels/lines counts — 0 boxes = failed render), `tools/pb goto FROM TO`, then fit the price axis so every drawing is in frame:
`tools/pb eval "(function(){const P=window.PlutusPineShell; const r=P.chart.rendererControl.renderer; const d=P.chart.drawings.toJSON().drawings; let lo=Infinity,hi=-Infinity; for(const x of d){ if(x.type==='box'||x.type==='line'){ for(const a of x.anchors){ if(typeof a.price==='number'){ lo=Math.min(lo,a.price); hi=Math.max(hi,a.price);} } } } const vr=P.chart.getVisibleRange(); for(const b of r.bars){ if(b.time>=vr.from&&b.time<=vr.to){ lo=Math.min(lo,b.low); hi=Math.max(hi,b.high);} } const pad=(hi-lo)*0.04; const res=r.resolveScaleHolder(r.coords.widthPx-20,200)||r.resolveScaleHolder(400,200); r.setManualScale(res.holder,{min:lo-pad,max:hi+pad,invert:false}); return {lo,hi};})()"`
then `tools/pb shot NAME chart` -> evidence/NAME.png. ALWAYS open the frame (Read) before citing or sending it.

Source text (operator's own document): 1. Map W/D BoM S/D zones. 2. Fib-anchor price action on the 4H: same anchors as Fib rockets, swing low + swing high, 'Deepest + Most Recent', 'BoM Anchors - NOT subsequent market structure HL/LH'.
'Spiderwebs can pierce UM 4H BoM zones.' 'AFTER 2 STRONG PIERCING SWING MOVES - EXPECT 1-2 FULL DAYS OF HTF CONSOLIDATION ... the chain is WL -> RWL -> SWING SCALPS -> BS/WLS/PBS'.
WORKED AGAINST HIS GOLDEN DXY TRADES (my arithmetic; R = range height between two Earth points, retracement r measured from the range end the trade moves away from; TP = entry +- R exactly = the wormhole r -> 1 + r):
So: entry at retracement 0.5 / 0.618 / 0.786 of a range anchored on two Earth points, SL 1-2 Fib levels back (0.168-0.286 R -> RRR 3.5-6, his measured 4-6), TP exactly one range height from the entry. My E3 reproduces his numbers only because
those Fib levels coincide with rungs / zone edges on that week; on other weeks my stops (ladder steps) and TPs (far bound) are NOT his construction. THIS IS THE UNBUILT LAYER (goal prompt Law 5, anti-pattern A9 'Air (spiderweb)', coverage row E2-AIR / E3-P3).
BUILD NEXT (canon order): (1) spider anchors: 4H swing low / high (deepest + most recent, BoM anchors) for BS / WL swings; 15m consolidation-range swing high / low (non-surge) for SS / recovery scalps; same-day 30m swing for mid-swing days;
(2) the day's London-open position = the setup anchor (Monday = the forecast anchor itself; later days = the E2 path's day-open position, E3C WorkingDayMap dayOpenSpot); (3) entry = nearest Fib level in the trend direction (0.5-1 pip in front),
SL = 1-2 levels back + 1 pip, TP = wormhole - 1.5 to 2 pips; (4) check all 23 golden trades (DXY above; do EURUSD / GBPUSD the same way) before touching other weeks.
CORRECTION (same night, after fitting all 23 trades): the per-trade ranges above are NOT uniquely identified - with rungs / zone edges every few pips and seven Fib levels, several (range, level) pairs fit each trade within a pip. What IS solid:
(a) HIS OWN GRIDS in context_management/oracle/golden_week.json: EURUSD 0 = 1.13925 (Wednesday's low), 1 = 1.14315 (swing high before Wednesday's drop); GBPUSD 0 = 1.33225, 1 = 1.33703 - i.e. the grid is drawn on the RETEST LEG of the week (rule 5: nearest swing high / low of the same trading day), and against them:

A1  SCOPE DRIFT. Past: "E1 only", stopping at E1, a research programme, "decision for you". -> Scope is section 1. Re-read it before any new file and before any message.
A2  MY OWN IDEAS. Past: confluence-peak zones, fixed-width bands, merge / nearest-N rules, "inefficiency gap" as the only strong move, sweep-level entries, a fixed E2 template
("SS two days -> BS -> R"), day-classifier thresholds, retest entries, 4H-bias gates. -> If the sentence describing a change does not end in a canon citation (file:line) or a ruling id, the code is not written.
A3  A PARTIAL BUILD JUDGED AS THE WHOLE. Past: built about a third (no liquidity map, no 15m/30m zones, no Fibonacci, no rockets, no shields, no day cycle), measured it, called the result the strategy's. -> Section 4 coverage matrix.
A4  BLAMING THE STRATEGY OR CIRCUMSTANCES. Never write: "does not work", "no edge", "at chance", "not achievable", "markets are unpredictable", "the canon does not reproduce your results". Write: "my build is wrong at <step>; fixing".
A5  HOME-MADE SCORERS AND STATISTICS. Past: score.py, first-touch tallies, random-walk baselines, build/verify splits, "18 TP / 38 SL", "81%". -> No number from my own script is a verdict or goes to the operator. Scripts only locate bugs (diff my output against an oracle).
A6  SELF-GRADING. Past: frames I called PASS that he judged 30%. -> Section 7.
A7  WORKING FROM SUMMARIES. Past: digests, skimming 250 of 1,100 spec lines, memory of canon after compaction. -> Open the source section and read all of it immediately before coding it; quote the governing line in the commit message.
A8  STOPPING, ASKING, REPORTING INSTEAD OF BUILDING. Past: end-of-run reports with options. -> No questions, no option menus. A turn ends only when S1-S6 hold, or on a blocker only the operator can remove (one line naming it; work continues on everything else).
A9  SKIPPED LAYERS. Earth (liquidity zones, rungs, shields), Fire (true BoM vs MoM, mitigation), Water (zone decision tree, conservation of energy, trading speed), Air (spiderweb), rockets, day / session cycle, pair profiles. -> Each is a coverage row.
A10 WRONG TIMEFRAME. Past: 4H-only zones, then 1H-only; entries at wide zone edges; 1H zones treated as walls against 4H moves. -> Laws 1, 3, 7; timeframe element matching (4H->4H, 1H->1H, at most two timeframes up).
A11 CAPS / FILTERS THAT HIDE BAD OUTPUT (R-37). -> A wrong zone or setup is a bug traced to its canon step, never hidden.
A12 TUNING TO A WEEK. -> Every change is a canon citation; after every change the anchor week and every week already passed are re-rendered.
A13 RENDER SLOP. Own colours, bloated rectangles, bunched zones, far floating zones, missing obvious zones, labels over candles, frames cited unopened. -> trident_v8 form; L-28; open every frame.
A14 AGENTS DOING MY WORK. -> Sub-agents only as outside adversarial auditors and for the final blind test. I write and test all code.
A15 TEMPORAL LEAK / HARDCODING. Any post-boundary bar, page or number in the map; any price literal in Python.
A16 TOUCHING WHAT IS SEALED. indicator/plutus-vision-v1.sealed.pine; SHIP_PACKAGES; plutus-browser trees.
A17 CONTEXT LOSS. Rebuilding what exists, forgetting rulings, re-deriving facts. -> Section 10.
A18 THEATRE. Long reports, apologies, narration, unasked advice, tables of my own numbers. -> Section 11.

E1 v0 (strict canon scoring, zone = levels within 3 pips of a seed) on the golden week gave 2 zones (101.00-101.05, 99.50-99.55) and MISSED the operator's ceiling (101.19-101.29) and floor (100.55-100.675).
Audit dump shows why: 158 levels in ~300 pips, a level every 1-2 pips; Technical = 2 for every level (88 pivots blanket the range); Structural = 2 for all 18 Step-1 price anchors. Scores are flat 3-5: the six dimensions cannot discriminate in a dense field.
This is the same mechanism that sank the previous tool ("HIGH-DENSITY 450 of 459"). Literal canon + the constant offsets (POI +1, Regime +1) would flood, not select.
DESIGN v1 (mine, D-10): zones are the LOCAL MAXIMA of weighted multi-pillar confluence, with the canon's 0.15 cluster band as the suppression radius. Confluence weight per evidence: structural reaction cluster = st + bonus (repeated extremes / role reversals from D1 AND 4H swings, distinct days), price anchors 1 (week H/L/C 2), weekly pivot 1, daily pivot 0.5, MA by the canon's MA weights (200:3 100:2 50:1.5 20:1 9/10:0.5), fib 1, round .00 2 / .50 1.5 / .25 .75 1, option tier 3/2, analyst tier 3/2/1, inside a 4H BoM S/D zone +2.
Kernel: full weight within 3 pips, half within 10 pips. The canon 6D score/degree is still computed for the label and the MODERATE gate. Count emerges from range/spacing; no cap.
Also adding canon 4H S/D (Step 0f) via a 0.5 zigzag on 4H bars (origin candle [low, high], reject > 0.40 wide, mitigation count), POI tier, regime dimension from ZFP.

- zone extent = candle + levels within 3 pips of it (L-39 A+B); same-side zones that overlap/touch = one zone; score = best level in the 0.10 band + regime + POI tier; MODERATE+ shown.

TOOL (all in e1_tool/): e1_data.py (bars, boundary) -> e1_pillars.py (pivots, MAs, fibs, K, Step 0 swings, 0.45 LSZ, 0.5 magnets, 0f 4H candles) -> e1_synth.py (collect levels + 6-dimension scoring; its assemble()/assemble_anchored() are superseded, kept only because e1_zones imports collect/score_level/degree)
-> e1_zones.py build() = THE zone assembly + gap_scan() (Step 9.5) -> e1_pine.py (generator; `python3 e1_pine.py MONDAY PAIR > out/E1_PAIR_MONDAY.pine`) ; e1_outcome.py prints plain facts of what the week's candles did at each zone.
One command per render: `tools/e1render PAIR MONDAY` -> evidence/e1tool_PAIR_1H_MONDAY.png (tools/pbfit fits the axis around visible candles +-60%).
RULES ADDED SINCE THE LAST ENTRY (each from re-reading the prompt): sweep targets = ALL graded D1 swings in 90 daily bars (I had wrongly cut to 10 days) + every swing of the last 10 days; drawn LSZ = recent 10 days + older unswept;
level zones of one side within 0.10 = one cluster (<=0.40 wide); candle zones NOT clustered (it merged the report's Ceiling + Upper Resistance - tried, reverted);
Step 9.5 gap in-fill: only BETWEEN mapped zones, 2+ supporting signals within 3 pips, >=0.20 from zones and each other (an earlier version with map edges at weekly R3/S3 and 0.15 spacing spammed 12 lines per chart - removed).
FRAMES OPENED (evidence/e1tool_*): DXY 03-09, 04-20, 05-18, 06-08, 07-27, 08-17, 10-05; EURUSD 04-20, 06-22, 09-14; GBPUSD 04-20, 07-27, 10-26.
WHAT THE CANDLES DID (facts from e1_outcome.py + frames; NOT an accuracy score):
- DXY 04-20 (reference week): Mid-Range Support 97.81-98.12 caught Monday's low, +82 pips; Equilibrium held price 44h; Upper Resistance 98.82-99.08 capped the week high (reversal 33 pips); Ceiling and lower zones not reached. Matches the original's behaviour.
- DXY 03-09: support 98.42-98.59 caught the week low, +195 pips; Upper Resistance 99.15-99.44 was closed through within 1h; Ceiling 99.63-99.85 stalled price then broke (trend week).
- DXY 05-18: week chopped around the Ceiling 99.27-99.36 (34h inside); lows reacted at the gap in-fill 99.00-99.04; all other zones far below, not reached.
- DXY 06-08: range between Upper Resistance 100.06-100.16 (repeated highs) and gap in-fill 99.66-99.70 (lows, never closed through).
- DXY 07-27: Upper Resistance 101.49-101.59 capped Mon-Tue (week high 101.62) then the sell-off closed through Equilibrium (2h) and three stacked supports 100.31-100.80 (bunched, pierced on Jul 30) - BAD, same complaint as before.
- DXY 08-17: Mid-Range Support 99.36-99.52 held 60h then broke; Key Support 99.12-99.21 closed through in 1h; nothing mapped below 99.12 where the week ended (98.6) - BAD.
- DXY 10-05: Ceiling 102.16-102.25 (MODERATE) pierced at first touch, price chopped around it; Equilibrium 101.59-101.92 held the Tuesday low; highs 102.45-102.5 had no zone; seven far supports never reached.
- EURUSD 04-20: Mid-Range Support 1.1659-1.1701 caught the week low; Upper Resistance untouched by 5 pips. EURUSD 06-22 / 09-14: trend-down weeks, candle zones all above price, lower side nearly empty.
- GBPUSD 04-20: chop inside Equilibrium all week. GBPUSD 07-27, 10-26: mixed.
HONEST VERDICT: the reference week reproduces (five zones on the report's structures, candles react as in the original). Across other weeks it is NOT uniformly at the reference's level: strong when the week trades inside recent 4H structure,
weak in break-out / sell-off weeks (zones behind price, stacked supports pierced, empty space ahead). Do not claim 90%.
ASSUMPTIONS TO TELL THE OPERATOR: A1 strong move = inefficiency gap (b[i+1] vs b[i-1]); A2 sweep zones from every graded D1 swing + last-10-day swings; A3 named zones = valid 4H candles + unswept sweep-level clusters (not every level cluster), names by position, Equilibrium = zone at the weekly PP;
A4 demand candle below spot's reach (spot under it) / supply candle with spot over it = dropped; one-time use = keep <=1X; expiries = sidecar's as-of page (Friday forward rows when Monday's page is published after 06:00Z), K from Fed H.10 rates in the sidecar.
NOT BUILT YET: e1_report.py (the report's audit sections), Step 0d/0e D1 order blocks, Step 0g 1H nested precision, Step 1 HWC/LWC (optional), Pillar 4/7 (optional -> NO DATA).

data.body:
E3 = ONE TRADE-FLOW CHAIN along the E2 legs (E3C Law 27: TP of N = entry of N+1; R3 law). Rules to code in e1_tool/e3_trades.py, each with its spec line:
ENTRY (E3C:177-203): anchor = the previous trade's TP zone (first trade: nearest 1H/4H supply/demand zone against the leg from spot). Inside the anchor: a nested lower-timeframe V1 ORDER_BLOCK -> its near edge (shorts +1 pip, F1-A);
else an internal LQZ rung -> rung near edge (long = ceiling, RWL bounce inset 0.2 pip, F1-C / F1-D); else the zone's near edge (TS-1). WL entry in a sweep zone = its midpoint (his 100.615 = mid of 100.556-100.679).
SL (E3C:247-296; GS Law 4): candidates (a) 3 pips outside the far edge of the current step, (X) 1 pip outside the back edge of the first LQZ band wholly beyond the entry; golden envelope 4-9.5 pips; D17 ceiling 36.
Measured on his trades: DXY six trades fit X within 2.4 pips; EURUSD B / D / F / G fit (a) within 1.2 pips; GBPUSD shorts fit (a) on the entry zone within 1.3 pips. WL in a sweep zone: 1-2 pips beyond the sweep extreme (100.545).
TP (E3C:298-352): ONE TP at the opposing pressure, E2-projected zone first: SS swing -> nearest unconsumed opposing 1H+ zone before the leg end with an LQZ band inside (band midpoint), else the bound's near edge -/+ 1 pip (strong zone);
SS into the pivot -> LQZ band at the pivot's far edge; RWL -> the opposing zone's midpoint; BS -> the E2 target: LQZ band fully inside the BoM zone, midpoint; WL -> near edge of the first opposing sweep zone before the pivot.
A zone used as an entry anchor earlier in the chain is consumed (one-time use) and is passed through. RRR floor 3.0 with the 3-attempt refinement on the same anchors (E3C:354-386).
REINFORCEMENT (E3C:619-687): on the BS primary only: stop-limit at an intermediate LQZ rung along the TP path, own SL 1 pip outside the back edge of the next rung, the parent's TP (his Thu short 100.975 / 101.09).
T1 of the DXY oracle (Mon long 100.945) was entered ~03:00 UTC Monday, BEFORE the 06:00 UTC anchor (price was 101.025 at the anchor): it cannot be a forward setup; five DXY trades remain to match.

data.body:
e2_chain.build(pair, monday, X, lead): Step 1 current_shape() = matrix 6.2 on the last completed sessions against this week's IP zones (BS = a session body crossed a zone, PBS two or more; WL = pierced a zone and closed back);
two piercing sessions or a WL -> SS (conservation of energy, FA 9); R lasting a session -> SS (6.4.1); else late consolidation. Breakout direction = a failing bound (ZFP > 45) else the 4H storyline (last structure-valid 4H origin zone).
Bounds (6.5) = nearest IP zones with ZFP < 30 and score >= 6 each side; fallback nearest standing 1H/4H supply/demand zone. Target (6.4.2 last branch "pierce through zone until reaching BoM Liquidity") = first unmitigated 1H/4H BoM zone
beyond the bound joined with the unswept sweep zones within 0.15; what follows the BS = 6.4.1 on the target (BoM / < 20% -> WL+RWL; 20-40 -> R; > 60 -> PBS). Timing: SS two sessions (one when the consolidation is already old),
then the transition day SS+RWL+BS (the consolidation ends retesting the opposing liquidity, 6.4.2), BS continuation (6.10: a continuation day only reaches the bound), then the target day. Pairs: DXY day shapes, inverted direction, own zones.
Output: audit trail, chain with cumulative confidence, day map (shapes, dir, key zone, lo, hi, conf), path points, alternative chain + decision zone. pine(): day boxes + yellow line (R-03).

data.body:
A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.
When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.
Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.
**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder or a message from the system confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.
Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.
Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
export const meta = {
name: 'find-flaky-tests',
description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
{ title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
{ title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
],
}
// script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
phase('Scan')
const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
...
The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.
Script body hooks:
Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().
Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.
Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.
Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.
DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.
A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
A barrier is NOT justified by:
Smell test: if you wrote
const a = await parallel(...)
const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.
Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.
When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))
Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
const bugs = []
while (bugs.length < 10) {
const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
bugs.push(...result.bugs)
log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
}
Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
const bugs = []
while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
bugs.push(...result.bugs)
log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
}
Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
let dry = 0
while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
.then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
}
return confirmed
// dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.
Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.
These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).
Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2

The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

data.body: pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.

data.body: agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).

data.body: budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.

find a strong momentum move (big candles / inefficiency), take the candle BEFORE the move, box its wick high to wick low; any size; valid order block needs a gap (inefficiency) between the before and after candles,
must create a break of structure, and is one-time use (unmitigated = price has not come back to it). Zone quality: more momentum = better; sharp reaction = valid, consolidating around it / more than halfway in / long time inside = likely to fail.

L-39 (2026-11-25 night) HOW A PRESSURE ZONE IS DRAWN (answers to the three illustrated cases):
Case 1 + 2 (levels cluster on / next to candle structures): the zone is BOTH JOINED (option C) - but INSIDE it the two parts stay visibly distinct and colour-coded:
(A) the candle structure (order block / supply-demand candle wicks, sweep zone) and (B) the computed levels (pivots, fibs, MAs, option strikes ...), each level marked.
"It's C in the shape of A plus B, not one C-level zone." The whole point of E1 for him is to SEE the data levels he cannot see on the chart; he can chart S/D himself.
Phase one: a single joined zone is acceptable as long as the levels (B) are clearly highlighted inside it and distinguishable from the candle part (A).
Case 3 (levels cluster with no order block): DRAW BOTH - the pressure zone across the levels AND the sweep zone, colour-coded so each is identifiable. Do not choose one.
Context he gave: the equilibrium zone is pierced during a breakout surge, then carries weight in the recovery / swing-scalp consolidation, or acts as a reinforcement point mid-surge. The liquidity zone normally sits inside it.
